title: Hubballi protest demands action over remarks on Basavanna

tea.why: Protesters condemned derogatory remarks about 12th-century social reformer Basavanna and statements concerning the Constitution.
tea.want: Demanded legal action and stringent punishment against the author, editor, and seer involved in the controversial remarks.
tea.changed: Nov 26: Protesters marched in Hubballi, burnt effigies, and submitted a memorandum addressed to the Chief Minister.

summary: Members of various people's organisations staged a protest in Hubballi on Thursday, condemning derogatory remarks about 12th-century social reformer Basavanna and statements concerning the Constitution. Organised by the Hubballi Janapara Sanghatanegala Okkoota, the demonstration began at the B.R. Ambedkar statue with the reading of the Constitution's Preamble on Constitution Day. Protesters then marched to the Tahsildar's office, where they burnt effigies of author Ravi Hanj, journalist Vishweshwar Bhat, and Adrushya Kadasiddeshwar Swami of Kanheri Mutt. The demonstrators demanded legal action against the author for claims made in his book and an interview, against the editor for publishing controversial material, and against the seer for remarks regarding the Constitution. The protest concluded with the submission of a memorandum addressed to the Chief Minister through the local Tahsildar, urging the formation of a special investigation team and restrictions on the author's entry into Karnataka.
demands: Register a case against author Ravi Hanj under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and IT Act
Form a Special Investigation Team supervised by a retired High Court judge
Impose restrictions on the author's entry into Karnataka
Investigate the involvement of others in the publication of the book
Condemnations and clarifications from Hindu organisations regarding the publication
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Protesters gathered at the B.R. Ambedkar statue in Hubballi to read the Preamble on Constitution Day and initiated a procession.
Demonstrators burnt effigies of an author, journalist, and a seer near the Tahsildar's office and submitted a memorandum.
